<reflection>
The first experiment provided fitting results with all NLL values relatively close, except M17 is somewhat worse. The top candidate is M2, but differences are small, meaning many mechanisms fit the single dataset similarly well. My aim for this turn is to design an experiment that discriminates among the leading candidates by probing the catalyst concentration dependence, which can separate mechanisms with monomeric vs. dimeric catalysis and also reveal deactivation effects.
</reflection>
<hypothesis>
The key mechanistic differences among candidates involve the order of the reaction in catalyst: some mechanisms (like M3 and possibly M5) require dimeric catalyst species for turnover, leading to quadratic scaling of initial rate with catalyst concentration, while most others have monomeric catalysis with linear scaling. Additionally, deactivation mechanisms (e.g., M9-M20) may show incomplete conversion or altered time-course shapes that depend on catalyst concentration. By running an experiment with the same substrate concentration but a 20-fold lower catalyst concentration (0.005 M), we can observe whether the rate scales linearly or quadratically and whether deactivation becomes more or less pronounced. This condition should strongly separate M3 (and possibly M5) from the rest due to dramatically slower rates if catalysis is second-order in catalyst. It will also test if deactivation is second-order (e.g., M13, M18, M19), which would become less significant at low catalyst, leading to more complete conversion relative to the high-catalyst run.
</hypothesis>
